response.text:
Recent work supports fine-grained evidence audits, although the closest methods come from summarization and relevance assessment rather than a validated recommendation-error taxonomy. [TofuEval (2024)](https://aclanthology.org/2024.naacl-long.251/) pairs sentence-level factuality labels with explanations and distinguishes unsupported information, misreferencing, faulty reasoning and opinion presented as fact. [Ramprasad et al. (2024)](https://aclanthology.org/2024.acl-long.677/) additionally identify plausible contextual inferences lacking direct evidence. Applied here: link each feedback claim to user ID, recommended item ID, rank and exact title/description spans; preserve compatibility and ownership as unknown when evidence is absent.

[PAIRS (2024; revised 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.16950) studies uncertainty-guided pairwise comparisons for ranking evaluation. A proposed adaptation for the twenty-user audit: annotate recent specific matches, apparent duplication, specification concerns and unidentified content separately; record explicit preferences between identifiable items. Measure inversion rate as contradicted ranked pairs divided by feedback-supported, comparable pairs. Report ties, abstentions and evidence coverage separately; never convert unidentified references into negative labels. These audit categories and measurements are proposed adaptations, not established findings from PAIRS.

Agreement needs independent checking. [Fröbe et al. (SIGIR 2025)](https://eprints.gla.ac.uk/352747/) find LLM assessors agree more with one another than with humans and can favor LLM-based rankers. [Agreement Metrics for LLM-as-Judge Evaluation (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00093) emphasizes explicit treatment of ties, invalid outputs and abstentions. Double-annotate feedback-to-item links and error labels; report raw agreement, a suitable chance-corrected statistic, adjudicated disagreements and abstention coverage. Keep these diagnostics separate from the fixed macro validation HR@10 selection metric.
